candidate_ledger.output_variable_reasoning: The friction factor cf is dimensionless by definition in fluid mechanics. The input variables are density (rho), dynamic viscosity (mu), pipe diameter (D), flow velocity (U), and roughness height (r). Density has dimensions of mass per volume, dynamic viscosity has dimensions of mass per length-time, diameter and roughness height are lengths, and velocity is length per time. The friction factor is dimensionless, so its SI exponents are all zero. The problem states the power of relative roughness height must be zero in the output formula, so the roughness height does not contribute to the dimension of cf.
